breaks.quote: To prune something, I had to kill it, which means ending it for good
breaks.why: The named idea 'pruning' gets a second name, 'kill', and the reader must work out that the two mean the same thing.

breaks.quote: So at the start of one year, I began to cut
breaks.why: A third word, 'cut' (also the heading 'Cutting What Still Matters'), is used for the same act before 'pruning' is named, so the reader has to track three labels.

breaks.quote: Killing hurts. Of all these things
breaks.why: The paragraph switches to 'Killing' as the main word, then the chapter returns to 'pruned', so the reader cannot tell which term to carry out of the piece.
